When I first started building cars, I noticed something that bothered me: the amount of stuff that got thrown away. Scrap metal, wood from crates, even the sawdust. It seemed crazy to pay for materials and then pay again to haul them off. So we started looking at every piece and asking, “What else could this be?” Wooden crates became floorboards. Metal cuttings turned into small parts. It wasn’t charity or cleverness — it was just plain arithmetic. Every dollar wasted was a dollar the customer would eventually have to pay. And once the men in the shop saw we were serious about it, they started coming up with ideas of their own, some of them better than anything I’d thought of.
